beats.narration_text: Last week, Gavia was a Python server hiding inside a desktop app. This week the Python is gone. The detector was rewritten in Rust, the download shrank by almost half, and it installs on Mac, Windows and Linux. This is Sai. But a rewrite has one job first: find the same loons. Here is how you prove it did.

show.event: the ask types in under 'Hello, Sai'
the rewrite and the size land as result lines
the parity line lands last and holds

props.segment: The Weights Were Never the Risk
props.command: Gavia 0.2.0 swapped its Python backend for a Rust core and ships on three systems. Before you congratulate me, tell me how I know it still finds the same loons. “Same weights” is not an answer.
props.runningText: checking the rewrite against what it replaced…
output: macOS · Windows · Linux, built by CI

beats.narration_text: So what changed. The old app froze a Python server into the bundle and talked to it over a local port, with a token. All of that is gone. The detector runs inside the app, and the interface calls it directly. The Mac download went from eighty-four megabytes to forty-five, and every change builds installers for all three systems.

show.event: the runtime pieces fill the first row
the port, the token and the old test suite complete the grid
the caption settles — one Rust core, in-process

props.caption: Replaced by one Rust core, in-process

beats.narration_text: Here is the trap. The model file is byte for byte the same, so it is tempting to call the answers the same. They are not guaranteed. The network only sees what the decoder and the resizer hand it. So before deleting the Python, the port wrote down every box it found on every validation photo, and made the Rust match them.

show.event: the question splits into two ways to trust a port
the model-file branch warns that the pixels can drift
the resolver names what was actually measured — the pixels

data.slideMeta: A REWRITE · THE SAME MODEL FILE
data.question: Same weights — so the same answers?

branches.detail: every box on every val photo, saved

resolver.label: The weights were never the risk
resolver.detail: accuracy was measured on Pillow's pixels: its resampling, its rounding, its JPEG reduction

data.ghostText: python_reference.json was written before the Python was deleted

beats.narration_text: Here is one thing it had to rebuild. Before resizing, Pillow shrinks a JPEG inside the decoder, by the largest of one, two, four or eight that keeps both sides at least six hundred and forty pixels. A Nikon frame from the validation set gets four. The Rust decoder's own shortcut picks eight. On fifteen of the twenty-six photos, it would have handed the model a different picture.

show.event: the ratio r typesets — two floored fractions
the reduction rule f appears beneath it
the Nikon frame is evaluated: r = 5, so f = 4

props.title: How far does the decoder shrink a photo first?
props.note: Pillow's JPEG draft(), rebuilt in Rust for 0.2.0. A 5568 × 3712 Nikon frame is kept at 1392 × 928.
props.conditions: w, h: JPEG size in pixels; 640: the model's input. Run on all 26 validation photos: 26 of 26 match Pillow 12.3.0. jpeg-decoder's own scale() differs on 15.

beats.narration_text: And it did. Both pipelines were re-run for this video on the same twenty-six photos. Python found thirty-two boxes above the shipped threshold; Rust finds all thirty-two, in the same places, confidences at most a point and a half apart. Precision and recall agree to four decimals. Average precision moved by a thousandth. It also scores the faintest guesses, where Rust has ninety to Python's eighty-nine.

show.event: Python's 32 boxes land first
Rust's 32 match them
the worst confidence gap fills in
the AP change closes the table at −0.0011

props.title: Python against Rust, on the same 26 photos
props.note: Recorded output, re-run 2026-09-25 on loonnet_v1 val: tests/parity.rs + examples/evaluate.rs at 78b383e, evaluate.py at 663feeb. P 0.9062, R 0.8788 in both.

beats.narration_text: One more number, because last week I said one loon in five goes unreported. This week's recall reads eighty-eight, not eighty. The model did not improve; the weights are byte-identical. The ruler changed. Last week's figure came from the training framework's own validator. This one is the app itself, at its shipped threshold. Twenty-nine of thirty-three loons found. Four missed.

show.event: one set of weights starts down a single track
it splits by who does the measuring
the two recalls land as badges — 0.879 and 0.800

tracks.label: the training validator
notes: still printed on the model card

beats.narration_text: The README now also says what Gavia is for: six required features. Detection is shipped. Counting is partly there, as per-photo counts, which Swara Joshi contributed this week and which survived the rewrite. A call classifier, shoreline change, underwater habitat and invasive plants have not started. Next is survey counting: a whole folder, one total, one CSV.

show.event: detection and counting fill in first
the four not-started features complete the grid
the caption names the next step

props.caption: Next: survey totals and a CSV export

beats.narration_text: So: one page. The Python is gone, and the app runs on three systems. The weights were never the risk; the pixels were, and the port rebuilt them. All thirty-two boxes came back. And the recall moved only because the ruler did.

show.event: the artifact card opens on the rewrite
the pixels line and the re-run line fill in
the ruler line closes it

props.artifactTitle: The Weights Were Never the Risk
artifactLines: The Python backend is gone. Detection runs in a Rust core inside the app, with no server, port or token; the Mac download fell from 84 MB to 45 MB, and CI builds installers for macOS, Windows and Linux.
The model file is byte-identical, so the risk was the pixels. The port rebuilt Pillow's resampling, rounding and JPEG draft factor, and froze Python's answers before deleting it.
Re-run for this video: all 32 of Python's boxes reproduce, worst confidence gap 0.0151. P 0.9062 and R 0.8788 match exactly; AP@0.5 moved from 0.8921 to 0.8910.
Recall at the shipped threshold is 29 of 33 — a different ruler from last week's 0.800, not a better model. Also new: Settings, Help, a loon icon and Swara Joshi's per-photo count.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. If you are about to port a model to another language, paste this first. The weights will not change, so ask what to freeze before the old code goes: its outputs on real inputs, every step that touches pixels before the network does, and the one number you expect to move. If you cannot say why it moves, you are not done.

show.event: the handoff prompt types in under 'Your turn.'
the three things to freeze stack as it fills
the last clause lands and the cursor holds

TIMING TRAP: the composition is 120 frames @30fps = 4.0s and fades to opacity 0 over its last 12 frames, while remotion_scenes.py freeze-extends a short render with tpad=stop_mode=clone, which would clone the FADED frame into seconds of black. Narration is held to 7 words so it finishes inside the card. './art run' will print a SKIN LINT line wanting ClaudeTitleOutro; it is wrong for this channel.
